data.name: Karna
data.gender_notes: Karna is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'karn' meaning 'body' or 'son'. In Hindu mythology, Karna was a great warrior known for his courage and loyalty to his brother Duryodhana during the Mahabharata war. The name Karna carries the meaning “Virtuous Warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Karna usually hope their child will grow to embody virtuous warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes inner strength and selfless devotion.
data.etymology: Karna belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Virtuous Warrior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Karna total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Karna" is recognized in both Hindu and Christian traditions. In Christian contexts, there isn't a direct significance or connection to the Hindu warrior Karna. Instead, the name may be given due to its meaning as 'son' or 'body'. It may also be a nod to the character Karna from the Old Testament, who was a friend and champion to King Saul and a great warrior in Israel's army.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name 'Karna' in the Christian context can represent a strong and loyal follower of God. It can also be a reminder that each person is a unique creation of God, the 'body' and 'son' of the Almighty. In the Hindu context, naming a child Karna can instill values of courage, loyalty, and honor. In both traditions, the name can serve as an inspiration to live a life of bravery, integrity, and devotion.
